subject: ba
title: Nature of Business
objectives: Define business, explain why it exists, and identify its major actors.
Distinguish the Traditional and Modern concepts of business, including Davis and Blomstrom's view.
Explain the four types of utility business creates: form, place, time and possession.
State the economic, social and human objectives of business.
Classify businesses by category (primary/secondary/tertiary), by size (MSME thresholds), and by ownership (private/public enterprises).
Define a stakeholder and explain the role of law and CAMA in business.
study:
Business is organised, repeated activity aimed at producing, exchanging or distributing goods and services in pursuit of a return — what separates it from mere 'busyness' is the presence of an economic element: a return of money, prestige or satisfaction. Its major actors are the entrepreneur (who identifies the opportunity and assumes the risk), managers (who plan, organise, lead and control), the workforce, and capital providers.

Key termTraditional Concept — business exists to maximise profit through production and marketing. Modern Concept — business exists to maximise consumer satisfaction, earning profit while upholding social responsibility. Davis and Blomstrom describe this modern view of society as an ecological one — concerned with the mutual relations between human populations and their environment.

Business performs its role by creating utility — the satisfaction derived from goods and services — in four forms: form utility (raw materials transformed into finished goods, e.g. timber into furniture), place utility (goods transported to where they're needed), time utility (goods stored until required), and possession utility (ownership transferred to the consumer).

Exam tipThe four utilities are a favourite exam target precisely because they sound similar — always tie each one to its trigger action: form=transform, place=transport, time=store, possession=transfer ownership.

Business objectives split into three categories. Economic objectives: profit maximisation, market expansion, cost reduction, business growth, productivity improvement. Social objectives: environmental protection, community development, ethical business practices, consumer protection, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). Human (employee) objectives: psychological safety, fair compensation, professional development.

Businesses are grouped into three broad categories: Primary (Extractive) — agriculture, mining, fishing; Secondary (Manufacturing) — construction and industrial processing; Tertiary (Services) — banking, education, transport. By ownership, businesses split into Private Enterprises (owned/managed by individuals — sole proprietorships, partnerships, limited companies, cooperatives) and Public Enterprises (owned/managed by government, such as a Water Corporation or a Television Authority).

Key termMSME classification (by size) — Micro: ≤10 employees, sales revenue under ₦25 million, assets under ₦5 million (excluding land/buildings). Small: 10–49 employees, sales ₦25m–₦100m, assets under ₦50m. Medium: 50–249 employees, sales above ₦100m, assets ₦50m–under ₦500m. Large: over 250 employees, sales above ₦500m, assets above ₦500m.

Choosing an ownership form is driven by capital requirement, market size, managerial capability, registration requirements, risk-bearing appetite, ease of ownership transfer, and access to factors of production. In Nigeria, company registration is governed by the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA). A stakeholder is any person, group or organisation with a vested interest in a business's decisions and activities — not just its shareholders, but employees, customers, suppliers, government and the surrounding community.
recap:
• Business = organised activity for an economic return; Traditional concept = profit-first; Modern concept (Davis & Blomstrom) = consumer satisfaction + social responsibility, an 'ecological' view.
  • Four utilities: Form (transform), Place (transport), Time (store), Possession (transfer ownership).
  • Objectives: Economic (profit, expansion, cost, growth, productivity) · Social (environment, community, ethics, CSR) · Human (safety, pay, development).
  • Categories: Primary (extractive) · Secondary (manufacturing) · Tertiary (services).
  • Ownership: Private Enterprises (individual-owned) vs Public Enterprises (government-owned, e.g. Water Corporation).
  • MSME thresholds: Micro <₦25m sales/≤10 staff · Small ₦25–100m/10–49 staff · Medium >₦100m/50–249 staff · Large >₦500m/>250 staff.
  • CAMA governs company registration in Nigeria; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or affecting the business.

quiz.q: Business is fundamentally distinguished from mere 'busyness' by the presence of:
opts: An economic element yielding a return such as money, prestige or satisfaction

quiz.q: According to the Traditional Concept of business, the main motto of business is to:
opts: Maximise market share with no regard to profit
Maximise profit through production and marketing of products
Maximise consumer satisfaction above all else
Serve only social causes with no profit motive

quiz.q: According to the Modern Concept of business, the central point is:
opts: Consumer satisfaction, with profit earned while maintaining social responsibility
Profit maximisation without regard to society

quiz.q: Davis and Blomstrom describe the modern view of society, as it relates to business, as:
opts: An ecological one, concerned with the mutual relations of human populations with their environment
